claim: Over 2000 lncRNAs have been identified in zebrafish through transcriptomic studies of early embryonic development and five adult tissues.
source: Transcriptomic studies of early embryonic development (Ulitsky et al., 2011; Pauli et al., 2012) and five adult tissues (Kaushik et al., 2013) have identified over 2000 lncRNAs in zebrafish (Dhiman et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple published studies that performed transcriptomic analyses.

claim: 727 zebrafish lncRNAs have been confirmed as non-coding based on ribosome occupancy patterns.
source: of which 727 have been confirmed as non-coding based on ribosome occupancy patterns (Chew et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a study that analyzed ribosome occupancy patterns.

claim: 24 bona fide lncRNAs were selected for mutant analysis based on synteny, sequence conservation, expression dynamics, and proximity to developmental regulatory genes.
source: For our mutant analysis we selected 24 bona fide lncRNAs based on synteny (conserved relative position on at least one other vertebrate genome), sequence conservation, expression dynamics (expression levels, onset and pattern) and proximity to developmental regulatory genes (see Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of selection criteria and reference to Table 1 which lists the selected lncRNAs.

claim: 32 deletion alleles were generated using CRISPR-Cas9 for 25 zebrafish lncRNAs.
source: we selected 25 zebrafish lncRNAs based on their conservation, expression profile or proximity to developmental regulators, and used CRISPR-Cas9 to generate 32 deletion alleles
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Table 1.

claim: 24 alleles removed regions containing transcription start sites (TSS-deletion; 244 bp to 736 bp).
source: 24 alleles removed regions containing transcription start sites (TSS-deletion; 244 bp to 736 bp)
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in Table 1 showing deletion sizes.

claim: Eight alleles fully or partially removed the gene (1 kb to 203 kb).
source: and eight alleles fully or partially removed the gene (1 kb to 203 kb) (Table 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by data presented in Table 1 showing deletion sizes.

claim: qRT-PCR analysis demonstrated an average reduction of 94 ± 6% in the levels of targeted lncRNA transcripts.
source: qRT-PCR analysis demonstrated effective reduction in the levels of the targeted lncRNA transcripts (average reduction of 94 ± 6%; Table 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data presented in Table 1.

claim: None of the 25 lncRNAs analyzed were essential for embryogenesis, viability or fertility.
source: our systematic mutant studies indicate that none of the 25 lncRNAs analyzed here are essential for embryogenesis, viability or fertility
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic analysis data presented in Table 1 and throughout the Results section.

claim: Altered transcription of neighboring genes was observed in some lncRNA mutants.
source: We observed altered transcription of neighboring genes in some mutants
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1–4.

claim: 10 out of 40 neighboring genes showed more than two-fold changes in expression in lncRNA mutants.
source: In particular, 10 out of 40 neighboring genes showed more than two-fold changes in expression
evidence: The claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1–4.

claim: cyrano is an evolutionarily conserved lncRNA.
source: cyrano is evolutionarily conserved lncRNA
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge about cyrano conservation.

claim: Morpholino studies suggested cyrano has essential functions during zebrafish embryogenesis.
source: based on morpholino studies, has been suggested to have essential functions during zebrafish embryogenesis (Ulitsky et al., 2011)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous morpholino study.

claim: cyrano has been suggested to act as a sponge (decoy-factor) for HuR during neuronal proliferation.
source: cyrano has also been suggested to act as a sponge (decoy-factor) for HuR during neuronal proliferation (Kim et al., 2016a)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: cyrano has been suggested to regulate miR-7 mediated embryonic stem cell differentiation.
source: regulate miR-7 mediated embryonic stem cell differentiation (Smith et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: cyrano has been suggested to control the level of miR-7 in the adult mouse brain.
source: and control the level of miR-7 in the adult mouse brain (Kleaveland et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Two cyrano mutant alleles were generated: cyranoa171 (TSS deletion) and cyranoa172 (gene deletion including the miR-7 binding-site).
source: We generated two mutant alleles that removed the TSS (cyranoa171) or the gene (cyranoa172), including the highly conserved miR-7 binding-site (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description in text and visual representation in Figure 2A,B.

claim: The expression level of oip5 was not affected in cyrano mutants.
source: The expression level of the nearby gene (oip5) was not affected in either of these mutants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1–4).
evidence: The claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1–4.

claim: cyrano mutants developed normally and were viable and fertile.
source: cyrano mutants developed normally and were viable and fertile
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic observations and data in Table 1.

claim: Morpholinos targeting cyrano induced non-specific phenotypes in both wild type and mutants.
source: The previously reported phenotypes, including small heads and eyes, heart edema, and kinked tails were found in both wild type and mutants (Figure 2C), demonstrating that the morpholino-induced phenotypes were non-specific.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing morpholino effects in both wild type and mutants as shown in Figure 2C.

claim: cyrano transcripts are not required for embryogenesis, viability or fertility.
source: These results reveal that cyrano transcripts or their evolutionarily conserved miR-7-binding site, are not required for embryogenesis, viability or fertility.
evidence: The claim is supported by the lack of phenotypes in cyrano mutants as shown in experimental data.

claim: gas5 is an evolutionarily conserved lncRNA (growth-arrest specific 5).
source: gas5 is an evolutionarily conserved lncRNA (growth-arrest specific 5) (Coccia et al., 1992)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and established knowledge.

claim: gas5 is highly expressed in early development.
source: that is highly expressed in early development (Figure 3B)
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: gas5 hosts several snoRNAs implicated in zebrafish development.
source: and hosts several snoRNAs implicated in zebrafish development (Higa-Nakamine et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Knockdown and knockout studies in cell culture have indicated that gas5 might act as a tumor suppressor.
source: Knockdown and knockout studies in cell culture (Ma et al., 2016) have indicated that gas5 might act as a tumor suppressor (Pickard and Williams, 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: gas5 has been suggested to exert effects at distant genomic sites.
source: and exert effects at distant genomic sites (Schneider et al., 1988)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The gas5a173 mutant allele removed sequences containing the TSS (−169 to +127) and resulted in complete elimination of gas5 expression.
source: Our gas5a173 mutant allele removed the sequences containing the TSS (−169 to +127) (Figure 3A) and resulted in complete elimination of its expression (Figure 3B and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 3A, 3B, and 3D.

claim: Expression of osbpl9 was increased by 50% in gas5a173 mutants.
source: Expression of the neighboring gene osbpl9, encoding a lipid-binding protein, was increased by 50% (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: gas5 lncRNA can act in trans to affect pten expression by sequestering specific microRNAs.
source: Previous studies have shown that gas5 lncRNA can act in trans to affect pten expression (ptena and ptenb in zebrafish) by sequestering specific microRNAs (Li et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: gas5 transcript can mimic Glucocorticoid Response Element and act as a decoy factor (riborepressor) for the Glucocorticoid Receptor (nr3c1)-mediated transcription.
source: Additionally, gas5 transcript can mimic Glucocorticoid Response Element and act as a decoy factor (riborepressor) for the Glucocorticoid Receptor (nr3c1)-mediated transcription (Kino et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: ptena was significantly upregulated in MZgas5a173 mutants at 1-dpf.
source: We analyzed the expression level changes of these genes in MZgas5a173 embryos (at 1-dpf) and found significant upregulation for ptena in MZgas5a173 mutants (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: gas5a173 mutants were indistinguishable from wild type, reached adulthood and were fertile.
source: Despite these changes in gene expression, gas5a173 mutants were indistinguishable from wild type (Figure 3C), reached adulthood and were fertile.
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic observations shown in Figure 3C and Table 1.

claim: Lnc-setd1ba is the zebrafish orthologue of human LIMT (LncRNA Inhibiting Metastasis).
source: Lnc-setd1ba is the zebrafish orthologue of human LIMT (Sas-Chen et al., 2016) (LncRNA Inhibiting Metastasis)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study establishing orthology.

claim: Human LIMT has been implicated in basal-like breast cancers.
source: which has been implicated in basal-like breast cancers
evidence: The claim is inferred from the citation to Sas-Chen et al., 2016.

claim: Lnc-setd1ba is expressed from a shared promoter region that also drives the expression of the histone methyltransferase setd1ba in opposite direction.
source: It is expressed from a shared promoter region that also drives the expression of the histone methyltransferase setd1ba in opposite direction (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by genomic structure shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The mouse homolog of setd1ba is essential for embryonic development.
source: whose mouse homolog is essential for embryonic development (Eymery et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2016b)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies in mouse.

claim: The lnc-setd1baa174 allele removed 3137 bp of the gene downstream of its TSS.
source: We removed the gene of lnc-setd1ba downstream of its TSS (3137 bp deletion) (lnc-setd1baa174).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description of the deletion and data in Table 1.

claim: In situ hybridization and qRT-PCR revealed absence of lnc-setd1ba expression in lnc-setd1baa174 mutants.
source: In situ hybridization and qRT-PCR revealed absence of lncRNA expression (Figure 4C and E)
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 4C and 4E.

claim: setd1ba was strongly upregulated during cleavage stages in lnc-setd1baa174 mutants.
source: and strong upregulation of setd1ba (Figure 4D and E) during cleavage stages
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 4D and 4E.

claim: setd1ba and rhoF were slightly upregulated at one-day post fertilization in lnc-setd1baa174 mutants.
source: and slight upregulation of setd1ba and the other neighboring gene rhoF at one-day post fertilization (1-dpf) (Figure 4E)
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Maternal-zygotic lnc-setd1baa174 mutants were indistinguishable from wild type, reached adulthood and produced normal progeny.
source: Despite these changes, maternal-zygotic lnc-setd1baa174 mutants were indistinguishable from wild type (Figure 4B), reached adulthood and produced normal progeny.
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic observations shown in Figure 4B and Table 1.

claim: Squint encodes a Nodal ligand involved in mesendoderm specification.
source: Squint encodes a Nodal ligand involved in mesendoderm specification (Pei et al., 2007; Heisenberg and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Previously studied squint insertion mutant alleles lead to delayed mesendoderm specification and partially penetrant cyclopia.
source: The previously studied squint insertion mutant alleles (squintHi975Tg 50 and squintcz35 51) lead to delayed mesendoderm specification and partially penetrant cyclopia (Dougan et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Morpholino and misexpression studies have suggested an additional, non-coding role for maternally provided squint.
source: Morpholino and misexpression studies have suggested an additional, non-coding role for maternally provided squint, wherein the squint 3'UTR mediates dorsal localization of squint mRNA, induces the expression of dorsal mesoderm genes, and is required for the development of dorsal structures (Gore et al., 2005; Lim et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The squinta175 deletion allele lacked most of the protein coding region and the 3'UTR, including the Dorsal Localization Element (DLE).
source: To investigate the non-coding roles of squint mRNA we generated a deletion allele (squinta175) that lacked most of the protein coding region and the 3'UTR, including the Dorsal Localization Element (DLE) implicated in maternal squint RNA localization (Gilligan et al., 2011) (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description and visual representation in Figure 5A.

claim: In the squinta175 allele, 525 bp (178 bp 5'UTR, 280 bp first exon and 67 bp of second exon) out of the 1592bp-long mature transcript remain in the genome.
source: In this allele 525 bp (178 bp 5'UTR, 280 bp first exon and 67 bp of second exon) out of the 1592bp-long mature transcript remain in the genome (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the description and visual representation in Figure 5A.

claim: The level of remaining squint transcript was greatly reduced (~90%) in squinta175 mutants.
source: In situ hybridization (Figure 5B) and qRT-PCR (Figure 5C) showed that the level of remaining squint transcript was greatly reduced (~90%).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qRT-PCR data shown in Figures 5B and 5C.

claim: MZsquinta175 embryos displayed partially penetrant cyclopia, similar to existing protein-disrupting squint alleles.
source: MZsquint a175 embryos displayed partially penetrant cyclopia, similar to existing protein-disrupting squint alleles (Figure 5D) (Pei et al., 2007; Heisenberg and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1997; Golling et al., 2002)
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic observations shown in Figure 5D and citations to previous studies.

claim: The defects proposed to be caused by interference with squint non-coding activity were not detected in MZsquinta175 embryos.
source: but the defects proposed to be caused by interference with squint non-coding activity (Gore et al., 2005) were not detected
evidence: The claim is supported by the absence of expected phenotypes in the mutant analysis.

claim: Control RNA, non-protein coding squint RNA, and squinta175 RNA did not cause any phenotypes and did not rescue MZsquinta175 mutants.
source: We found that in contrast to wild-type squint mRNA, control RNA, non-protein coding squint RNA or squint a175 RNA did not cause any phenotypes and did not rescue MZsquint a175 mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by injection experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5–S1.

claim: squint 3'UTR does not have the previously proposed non-coding functions.
source: These results indicate that squint 3'UTR does not have the previously proposed non-coding functions
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing lack of non-coding activity.

claim: The squint transcript may not be a member of the cncRNA family.
source: and that the squint transcript may not be a member of the cncRNA family
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing lack of non-coding activity.

claim: Lnc-phox2bb neighbors phox2bb and smtnl1.
source: Lnc-phox2bb neighbors phox2bb and smtnl1.
evidence: The claim is supported by genomic location data shown in Table 1 and Figure 6A.

claim: Phox2bb is a transcription factor implicated in the development of the sympathetic nervous system.
source: Phox2bb is a transcription factor implicated in the development of the sympathetic nervous system (Pei et al., 2013), (Moreira et al., 2016; Tolbert et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: smtnl1 has been implicated in smooth muscle contraction.
source: while smtnl1 has been implicated in smooth muscle contraction (Borman et al., 2009)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Whole-gene deletion of lnc-phox2bb (lnc-phox2bba177) led to jaw deformation and failure to inflate the swim-bladder.
source: Whole-gene deletion of lnc-phox2bb (lnc-phox2bba177) (Figure 6A) led to jaw deformation and failure to inflate the swim-bladder (Figure 6B)
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic observations shown in Figure 6B.

claim: No homozygous lnc-phox2bba177 mutant fish survived to adulthood.
source: and no homozygous mutant fish survived to adulthood
evidence: The claim is supported by viability data shown in Table 1.

claim: The TSS-deletion allele (lnc-phox2bba176) lacked lnc-phox2bb RNA but TSS-deletion mutants developed normally and gave rise to fertile adults.
source: Like the whole-gene deletion allele, the TSS-deletion allele (lnc-phox2bba176) lacked lnc-phox2bb RNA (Figure 6E), but in contrast to the whole-gene deletion mutants, TSS-deletion mutants developed normally and gave rise to fertile adults.
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 6E and phenotypic observations in Table 1.

claim: The anterior expression domain of phox2bb in the hindbrain was absent in the lnc-phox2bb whole-gene deletion allele.
source: We found that the anterior expression domain of phox2bb in the hindbrain was absent in the whole-gene deletion allele (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The deleted region in lnc-phox2bba177 contains enhancer elements for phox2bb.
source: This finding is consistent with the observation that the deleted region contains enhancer elements for phox2bb (McGaughey et al., 2008)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and histone mark data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The deleted region in lnc-phox2bba177 contains conserved non-coding elements (CNEs).
source: conserved non-coding elements (CNEs) (Hiller et al., 2013) (Figure 6C)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and CNE data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The deleted region in lnc-phox2bba177 contains histone marks related to enhancer regions (H3K4me1 and H3K27Ac).
source: and histone marks related to enhancer regions (H3K4me1 and H3K27Ac) (Bogdanovic et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study and histone mark data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The expression level of smtnl1 increased in lnc-phox2bb gene deletion mutants relative to the TSS-deletion mutant and wild type.
source: We also found that the expression level of smtnl1 increased in gene deletion mutants relative to the TSS-deletion mutant and wild type (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: lnc-phox2bb RNA is not required for normal development.
source: These results indicate that lnc-phox2bb RNA is not required for normal development
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison between TSS-deletion and gene deletion phenotypes.

claim: The lnc-phox2bb locus overlaps with regulatory elements required for proper expression of phox2bb and smtnl1.
source: but that the lnc-phox2bb overlaps with regulatory elements required for proper expression of phox2bb and smtnl1 (Figure 6E)
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential phenotypes and expression changes between TSS-deletion and gene deletion alleles.

claim: Absence of putative DNA regulatory-elements at the lnc-phox2bb locus, but not of the lncRNA transcript itself, resulted in abnormal development.
source: In one case (lnc-phox2bb), absence of putative DNA regulatory-elements, but not of the lncRNA transcript itself, resulted in abnormal development.
evidence: The claim is supported by the differential phenotypes between TSS-deletion and gene deletion alleles shown in Figure 6.

claim: The majority of individual zebrafish lncRNAs have no overt roles in embryogenesis, viability and fertility.
source: but extrapolation from our results suggests that the majority of individual zebrafish lncRNAs have no overt roles in embryogenesis, viability and fertility
evidence: The claim is inferred from the systematic analysis of 25 lncRNAs showing no essential functions.

claim: LncRNAs might have redundant, subtle, or context-dependent roles.
source: LncRNAs might have redundant, subtle, or context-dependent roles
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning about potential explanations for the lack of overt phenotypes.

claim: Visual assessment of live embryos and larvae is a powerful and efficient approach to identify mutant phenotypes.
source: Previous large-scale screens (Driever et al., 1996; Haffter et al., 1996) have shown that the visual assessment of live embryos and larvae is a powerful and efficient approach to identify mutant phenotypes
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous large-scale screening studies.

claim: No notable abnormalities were detected in 31/32 lncRNA mutants.
source: No notable abnormalities were detected in 31/32 mutants.
evidence: The claim is supported by phenotypic screening data shown in Table 1.

claim: 31 out of 32 lncRNA mutants survived to adulthood.
source: Moreover, these 31 mutants survived to adulthood, indicating functional organ physiology
evidence: The claim is supported by viability data shown in Table 1.

claim: 31 out of 32 lncRNA mutants were fertile.
source: and were fertile (Table 1)
evidence: The claim is supported by fertility data shown in Table 1.

claim: LncRNAs have been proposed to affect the expression of neighboring or distant genes by acting as signaling, guiding, sequestering or scaffolding molecules.
source: LncRNAs have been proposed to affect the expression of neighboring or distant genes by acting as signaling, guiding, sequestering or scaffolding molecules (St Laurent et al., 2015; Rinn and Chang, 2012; Nagalakshmi et al., 2008; Carninci et al., 2005; Kapranov et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies proposing these mechanisms.

claim: The functions of specific lncRNAs in dosage compensation (xist, tsix, jpx) are well established.
source: The functions of specific lcnRNAs in dosage compensation (xist (Brockdorff et al., 1991; Marahrens et al., 1997), tsix (Lee et al., 1999), jpx (Johnston et al., 2002)) and imprinting (Airn (Wutz et al., 1997; Latos et al., 2012), MEG3 (Miyoshi et al., 2000; Kobayashi et al., 2000), H19 (Bartolomei et al., 1991; Feil et al., 1994)) are well established
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies establishing these functions.

claim: The functions of specific lncRNAs in imprinting (Airn, MEG3, H19) are well established.
source: and imprinting (Airn (Wutz et al., 1997; Latos et al., 2012), MEG3 (Miyoshi et al., 2000; Kobayashi et al., 2000), H19 (Bartolomei et al., 1991; Feil et al., 1994)) are well established
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to multiple studies establishing these functions.

claim: Mutant studies in mouse have suggested that fendrr, peril, mdget, linc-brn1b, and linc-pint are essential for normal development.
source: and mutant studies in mouse have suggested that fendrr, peril, mdget, linc-brn1b, linc-pint (Sauvageau et al., 2013), and upperhand (Anderson et al., 2016) are essential for normal development
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous mouse mutant studies.

claim: Other studies have questioned the developmental relevance of several mouse lncRNAs, including Hotair, MIAT/Gumafu, Evx1-as, upperhand, braveheart and haunt.
source: However, other studies have questioned the developmental relevance of several mouse lncRNAs, including Hotair (Amândio et al., 2016), MIAT/Gumafu (Ip et al., 2016), Evx1-as (Bell et al., 2016), upperhand, braveheart and haunt (Han et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies questioning lncRNA functions.

claim: Morpholinos targeting megamind and cyrano resulted in embryonic defects in zebrafish.
source: In zebrafish, morpholinos targeting the evolutionarily conserved lncRNAs megamind (TUNA (Lin et al., 2014)) and cyrano resulted in embryonic defects (Ulitsky et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous morpholino study.

claim: A mutant study found no function for megamind and revealed that a megamind morpholino induced non-specific defects.
source: However, a mutant study found no function for megamind and revealed that a megamind morpholino induced non-specific defects (Kok et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous mutant study.

claim: There is a controversy about the importance of lncRNAs for vertebrate development.
source: These conflicting results have led to a controversy about the importance of lncRNAs for vertebrate development (Sauvageau et al., 2013), (Han et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies representing different perspectives on lncRNA importance.

claim: lncRNA promoters can affect the expression of nearby genes in mammalian cell culture systems.
source: Previous observations in mammalian cell culture systems suggested that lncRNA promoters can affect the expression of nearby genes (Engreitz et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous cell culture study.

claim: The observations that lncRNA promoters can affect nearby gene expression hold true in vivo in zebrafish.
source: To test if these results hold true in vivo, we measured the changes in the expression of neighboring genes (a 200 kb window centered on each lncRNA) in lncRNA mutants. Several mutants displayed changes in the expression of neighboring genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1–4). In particular, 10 out of 40 neighboring genes showed more than two-fold changes in expression, lending in vivo support to observations in cell culture systems (Engreitz et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing neighboring gene expression changes in vivo.

claim: cyrano has been suggested to have functions in brain morphogenesis.
source: and brain morphogenesis (Sarangdhar et al., 2018)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The TSS-mutant allele of cyrano lacked the e1i1 morpholino-binding site.
source: The TSS-mutant allele lacked the e1i1 morpholino-binding site
evidence: The claim is supported by the genomic structure shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The gene deletion allele of cyrano lacked the CMiBS morpholino-binding site.
source: and the gene deletion allele lacked the CMiBS morpholino-binding site (Figure 2A)
evidence: The claim is supported by the genomic structure shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The evolutionarily conserved miR-7-binding site in cyrano is not required for embryogenesis, viability or fertility.
source: These results reveal that cyrano transcripts or their evolutionarily conserved miR-7-binding site, are not required for embryogenesis, viability or fertility.
evidence: The claim is supported by the lack of phenotypes in cyrano gene deletion mutants that lack the miR-7 binding site.

claim: The role of gas5 lncRNA in development has not been studied in any vertebrate prior to this study.
source: However, the role of this lncRNA in development has not been studied in any vertebrate.
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of cited studies on gas5 developmental roles in vertebrates.

claim: TL/AB zebrafish were used as wild-type fish in this study.
source: TL/AB zebrafish (Danio rerio) were used as wild-type fish in this study.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the experimental methods.

claim: Fish were maintained on daily 14 hr (light): 10 hr (dark) cycle at 28°C.
source: Fish were maintained on daily 14 hr (light): 10 hr (dark) cycle at 28°C.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the experimental methods.

claim: At least 15 adult homozygous mutant pairs per allele were crossed to test fertility of mutants and to generate maternal and zygotic mutants.
source: At least 15 adult homozygous mutant pairs per allele were crossed to test fertility of mutants and to generate maternal and zygotic mutants (MZ) devoid of maternally and zygotic lncRNA activity.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the experimental methods.
